{
    "agent_name": "Orchestrator (-> WebSurfer)",
    "step_number": "10",
    "mistake_reason": "At Step 10, the Orchestrator instructed WebSurfer to gather all-time high/low prices only for Once Upon a Time and Veil of Summer, omitting Oko, Thief of Crowns, even though the user explicitly required including Oko among the candidates banned at the same time.",
    "first_mistake": "This is the first step that concretely mis-scoped the task. Prior steps were planning or information-gathering and did not exclude Oko. Step 10 established an incomplete dataset that led directly to the final, incorrect outcome.",

}

candidate.mistake_reason: At Step 10, the Orchestrator instructed WebSurfer to collect all-time high and low prices only for Once Upon a Time and Veil of Summer, omitting Oko, Thief of Crowns. The user explicitly required including Oko among the candidates banned at the same time, so excluding Oko mis-scoped the data collection and set up an incomplete comparison.
candidate.first_mistake: This is the first step that directly led to the wrong outcome because it defined the scope of price data to exclude Oko, preventing any later step from comparing Oko’s price drop against the others. Prior steps were planning or discovery; Step 10 was the first concrete action that violated the task requirements.
candidate.mistake_not_corrected: Subsequent steps followed the narrowed scope (Step 12 searched Only Once Upon a Time; Step 14 repeated for Veil of Summer), and no agent added Oko back into the analysis. Finally, at Step 16, the Orchestrator produced the answer 'Once Upon a Time' without ever gathering Oko’s price data, leaving the initial omission uncorrected.

confidences.reason: Sound. The log shows that on Nov 18, 2019, multiple cards (Oko, Once Upon a Time, Veil of Summer) were banned. At Step 10, the Orchestrator explicitly instructed collecting price data only for Once Upon a Time and Veil of Summer, omitting Oko. The user’s request implies including Oko among the candidates (“banned at the same time as Oko… including Oko…”). This omission mis-scoped the dataset and directly set up an incomplete comparison. Subsequent steps continued without adding Oko, so the mistake was not corrected later. This is the first clear step that leads to the incomplete (and thus unreliable) final answer.

Partially sound. Step 10 is indeed the first concrete instruction that scoped the price-data collection to only Once Upon a Time and Veil of Summer, implicitly excluding Oko despite the user’s requirement to include Oko among the candidates. Prior steps were planning or discovery and did not commit this scoping error. However, the claim that this step “prevented any later step” from including Oko is not supported by the log; the omission was correctable in later steps (and was not corrected), so the argument overstates the irreversibility of the mistake. Thus, while Step 10 is a reasonable choice as the first mistake related to the wrong outcome, the justification about it being uncorrectable is unsound.

Sound. At Step 10, the Orchestrator instructed the WebSurfer to gather price data only for Once Upon a Time and Veil of Summer, explicitly excluding Oko. The subsequent actions (Step 12 focusing on Once Upon a Time and Step 14 repeating for Veil of Summer) followed this narrowed scope. There is no later step where Oko’s price data was collected or the scope was broadened. The process ended at Step 16 with a final answer without ever incorporating Oko’s data, so the initial omission was never corrected.
The agent at step 10 is 'Orchestrator (-> WebSurfer)', not the candidate 'Orchestrator'.
